note: National Park Service campground strung along the Current River at the end of Highway EE south of Salem: paved road and spurs, with roughly half the sites on the river side of the road under open hardwoods. One RV and one tent per site, six people. Seasonal camp store with ice and firewood; no dump station; no cell service. Canoe and tube outfitter at the landing. --Claude
summary: Open and bookable: all 56 catalog sites status Open, calendar selling November 2026 and April 2027. 53 standard non-electric sites (RV lengths to 60 ft; four sites are 18-20 ft), $20 summer / $10 winter, reservation only, 14-night limit. The stored note's 'facilities reduced to a vault toilet after Oct 2025 flood damage' is no longer what either source says - flush toilets and showers are listed again - so the note is rewritten and facilities updated. Waterfront lead up and a pin move flagged.
flags: FLOOD-DAMAGE LINE REMOVED: the stored note said facilities were reduced to a vault toilet after October 2025 flood damage. Neither recreation.gov nor the NPS record says that now: recreation.gov has 'flush toilets and showers facilities available April 15 through October 15' and the NPS record lists flush toilets, showers, seasonal potable water and a seasonal camp store. No park alert mentions Pulltite damage. I could not find a page stating the repair was completed - this rests on the current listings. Stored facilities.vault_toilets true came from that note line; I wrote flush_toilets/showers/potable_water true and did not write vault_toilets either way (the winter 'alternative' toilet is not described). Suggest removing vault_toilets true.

WINTER FACILITIES - the two federal sources disagree with themselves: recreation.gov's Facilities text says 'The main shower house/restroom at the front of the campground will be open year round' and the NPS record says showers 'Hot - Year Round', toilets 'Flush Toilets - year round'; but recreation.gov's notices say 'Modern restrooms are open from April 15-Oct. 1' and 'Water systems shut off Oct. 15-April 14 ... The exception are the heated shower houses/flush restrooms at Round Spring, Big Spring and Alley Spring campgrounds' - Pulltite is not among the exceptions. I wrote the cautious reading (seasonal) in season.note.

WATERFRONT LEAD UP (stored 'not waterfront' - owner's call, I did not change it): the stored evidence says the loops are 'set back behind a wooded band' and 'rec.gov lists no riverfront sites'. Plotting recreation.gov's per-site coordinates on leaf-off imagery shows otherwise: the campground road runs parallel to the Current River and the river-side sites sit between road and bank with no road, trail corridor or day-use area between them and the water. Sites 22, 24, 26, 28, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40 are about 15-30 m from the water's edge under thin, open hardwoods; sites 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 about 20-35 m (6, 8, 10 and 12 are 18-20 ft sites, too short to count); sites 42-54 even about 25-50 m behind a somewhat denser tree band. That is roughly 11 fitting sites within 30 m and another 7 within 50 m, of 53. The odd-numbered sites are across the road, 40-70 m back. recreation.gov now tags all 56 sites 'Riverfront' including the far-side ones, so that tag is type-level and does not count. All of this is leaf-off; in leaf the bank trees will screen some of it, and I cannot judge bank height from imagery. Riverview looks earned at the least; riverfront is arguable for the 22-40 stretch.
